messages.author: 55e546e375e22a40
messages.subject: additive qtl
parts:
Hi,
Am doing qtl mapping using the marker regression method. I then run
another scan using the largest qtl as an additive covariate. I
expected to see the second largest peak (if it is not linked to the
largest peak) as the additive qtl, but this is not the case. Often the
additive qtl is none of the qtls returned from scan one. Is it
possible there is a problem with my map or is my assumption wrong?
Musa.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] additive qtl
parts:
It's impossible to say whether there is a problem with your genetic map or not, and it's hard to say whether the results you are seeing are surprising or not. How strong are the effects?

There is no guarantee that the second-highest peak will come up as most interesting once you condition on the first peak. I would look at both the effect of that second-highest locus and also the association between genotypes at the two loci.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: additive qtl
parts:
Genotypes at markers on different chromosomes would be expected to be
independent. If the genotypes at the highest and 2nd highest peaks
are associated, that may indicate a problem with the genetic map, or
there could be something else going on, but in any case it explains
why, after conditioning on the highest peak, the evidence for a QTL at
the 2nd highest peak goes away.

karl
